title: ks1370 integration pin: run its nine cells on a migrated PostgreSQL (superuser plus app role) and record the result (G243-N3)
description:

This ticket is the run: execute the file's nine cells on a migrated PostgreSQL and record the result here. It is a run, not a defect, and Low by Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 106th, finding G243-N3). The PR merged under the project's tested-work merge rule with the pre-merge tests not run; the change is a test file and two docs fragments with no product line.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, the PR 2071 section ("NOT TESTED, and this is the main gap: the nine cells were NOT run green"), head `697226c8395d`, verdict GO WITH NOTES.

The script is at line 13 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/package.json` and runs `vitest run --config` with the file `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/vitest.integration.config.ts`. The default config excludes every file whose name ends in `.integration.test.ts` (line 15 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/vitest.config.ts`), so the default run never picks the file up, and without the two URLs the file fails in its setup with a named error (the gate tested that half).

This run does not close KS-1370 or KS-1377: the header (lines 17 to 19) lists what the file does not prove, among them pgbouncer, the gateway cache, two OS processes and any box.

title: ks1370 pin B2 carries no may-change mark, and its 4 s window can flake under load (F-2071-1, F-2071-2)
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2071 (KS-1370, merged 2026-11-08T21:01:40Z as `425ea1d3df0f`) added one integration test file. Its cell B2 pins a window in the security service's boot probe, and the gate found two Minor notes on that one cell. F-2071-1: B2 pins today's behaviour (the database answers, the availability flag is still down, and a validate reads the stored row and warms memory), but the cell carries no mark that a later fix may change it, so a fixer who changes that window would see B2 go red and read it as a regression. F-2071-2: B2 depends on a 4 s window between the second failed retry and the third probe; if the event loop stalls, the retry timer could fire first, flip the flag, and fail the cell's `flagAtWarm` read. Both are Low by Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 106th point 1, findings G243-F5 and G243-F6). One ticket, two items: one cell, one test file, one gate pass. Neither item is a product defect, and F-2071-2 is unmeasured.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, the PR 2071 section, findings F-2071-1 and F-2071-2 on head `697226c8395d`, verdict GO WITH NOTES (the pin was not executed), accepted at merge.

## Item 1: F-2071-1 (Minor, READ ONLY)

The cell is at line 324 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/__tests__/ks1370-two-replicas-and-a-real-boot-race.integration.test.ts` at develop `425ea1d3df0f`: "pin B2: the database answers, the flag is still down, and a validate reads the stored row and warms memory". The file header (line 2) says the whole file is "A PIN OF BEHAVIOUR THAT DEVELOP ALREADY HAS, NOT A FIX", which partly mitigates the note. The cell's own title and its asserts (lines 325 to 330) carry no mark that this particular behaviour is one the tickets (KS-1370, KS-1377) might change.

## Item 2: F-2071-2 (Minor, READ ONLY, flakiness UNMEASURED)

The setup (lines 273 to 284 of the same file) waits for two failed retries (a `waitFor` with a 20 s budget, line 277), opens the relay, then reads `inst.db.isDbAvailable()` into `seen.flagAtWarm` at line 279; the cell asserts it is `false` at line 325. The comment at lines 274 and 275 gives the backoff as 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, so the third probe is 4 s after the second failed retry; the delay doubles at line 154 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/db.ts`. If a stalled event loop lets that timer fire between `relay.open()` and the read (the gate saw host load1 reach 15), the flag flips and the assert fails. The gate did not measure flakiness; no failing run is known.

## What I read

READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `425ea1d3df0f`): the lines cited above in the test file and in `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/db.ts`. The file has 349 lines and nine cells. I did not run it, and the gate did not either.

## Fix shape

The verdict gives none. My reading, not the gate's: item 1 is a one-line mark on the cell; item 2 starts with a measurement (run the file repeatedly under load) before any change.

## Related

KS-1370 (In Progress, PR 2071's ticket, left as is). KS-1377 (validate route follow-ups from the KS-1370 gate, not touched). The nine-cell run (G243-N3) is filed as its own ticket from the same gate pass.

title: ks1560 jq-link census predicate: legitimate ln spellings judged no link, and a trailing comment naming bin/jq passes (F-2078-1, F-2078-2)
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2078 (KS-1560, merged 2026-11-08T20:07:15Z as `93028c8151ec`) made the jq-link census read the link statement. Its one predicate, `links_jq` in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1560_private_path_suites_link_jq.test.sh`, is a single regex, and the gate found two edges on it. F-2078-1: legitimate spellings of the same `ln` statement are judged "no link", so a correct suite is reported as an offender (fails closed). F-2078-2: a trailing comment that names `bin/jq` on any `ln -s` line passes (a false ACCEPT). Both are Minor and both are Low by Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 106th point 1, findings G243-F3 and G243-F4; ADDENDUM to the board seat 2026-11-08T20:11:01Z). One ticket, two items: one regex, one test file and one test pass prove both. Nothing is wrong on today's tree.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, the PR 2078 section, findings F-2078-1 and F-2078-2 on head `e702127f3790`, verdict GO WITH NOTES, accepted at merge.

## Item 1: F-2078-1 (Minor, fails closed)

MEASURED by the gate (positive control `ln -sf "$JQ_BIN" "$root/bin/jq"` judged yes): the predicate needs the line to START with `ln`, to carry a flag word with an `s`, and to END with `bin/jq`, an optional quote, then the end of the line or one of `;&|#`. Judged NO link, so an offender is reported: `ln -sf "$JQ_BIN" "$root/bin/jq" 2>/dev/null`, the same with `>/dev/null`, `mkdir -p "$root/bin" && ln -sf ...`, `if ! ln -sf ...; then`, `( ln -sf ... )`, `command ln -sf ...`, `ln --symbolic --force ...`, a backslash-continued `ln`, and a destination directory ending `bin/`. Judged link: the plain shapes and `ln -s -f`, `--`, `${root}`.
Effect: a future suite that writes the link with `2>/dev/null` reddens this census suite. The suite runs in leg 14 (run-shell-suites), which gates the push. The PR's own NOT DONE names only `cp` and `install`.

## Item 2: F-2078-2 (Minor, false ACCEPT)

MEASURED by the gate: `ln -sf "$DOCKER_BIN" "$root/bin/docker"  # jq is at $root/bin/jq` is judged a jq link, because `bin/jq` followed by the end of the line satisfies the tail anchor; so does `; echo "$root/bin/jq"`, and `ln -sf "$root/bin/jq" "$stub/elsewhere" # bin/jq`. A trailing comment (or a trailing word) naming `bin/jq` on any `ln -s` line passes. The PR's fixtures cover the leading-comment and the source-only shapes, not these. It is narrower than the old "the words anywhere in the file" check and strictly better than develop was.

## What I read

READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `93028c8151ec`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1560_private_path_suites_link_jq.test.sh`): the regex is line 42; the comment at lines 37 and 38 itself says the destination may be "optionally followed by `||`, `;`, `&&` or a comment", which is the F-2078-2 edge; the call is line 51 and the census check is line 67; the fixtures start at line 69. The gate's probes are not re-run by me.
Also in the verdict, not an item here: the extractor in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1347_proxy_out_dir_spaced_checkout.test.sh` does not handle two OUT_DIR statements or a semicolon inside a string; the READY states it and the gate did not test it further.

## Fix shape

The verdict gives none.

title: Compose checker exits 2 on an ordinary PORT_OFFSET line (export, readonly, echo, if test): the unread filter is too narrow (F-2070-2)
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2070 (KS-2079, merged 2026-11-08T19:23:21Z as `5d6a95c552fd`) taught the compose checker to refuse a PARTIAL port list. Its new `unread` filter refuses to run (exit 2, "CANNOT RUN") on any non-comment line that mentions `PORT_OFFSET` and is neither the definition nor a `NAME=$(( N + PORT_OFFSET ))` line. So an ordinary new line such as `export PORT_OFFSET` or an `echo` of it would stop the checker, and the guard that calls it, until the regex is taught. The refusal is loud and names the line, so Minor; no verdict changes on the current tree. Low is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 106th, point 1, finding G243-F2).

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, finding F-2070-2 (Minor) on PR 2070, head `0ae8aa98046c`, verdict GO WITH NOTES, accepted at merge.

## Evidence

MEASURED by the gate (it ran the PR's three regexes verbatim against the real `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` plus one appended line; control: the real file refuses 0 lines):

* Refused: `export PORT_OFFSET`, `readonly PORT_OFFSET`, `echo "slot offset $PORT_OFFSET" >&2`, `if (( PORT_OFFSET > 900 )); then exit 1; fi`.
* Accepted: a trailing comment after a shape line, `SECUURA_PORT_OFFSET=3` (word boundary), `$((9999+PORT_OFFSET))` without spaces.
* Refused as intended: `export NAME=...`, reordered operands, an indented line, a lower-case name, a continuation split.

READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `5d6a95c552fd`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-compose-stack-safety.mjs`): the filter is at line 66 (`/\bPORT_OFFSET\b/` and not a comment and not a `PORT_OFFSET=` definition and not the `SHAPE` regex at line 65), the refusal at lines 67 to 70 ("CANNOT RUN: ... use PORT_OFFSET in a shape this derivation does not read").

## Fix shape

The verdict gives none. The choice to make is which non-assignment uses of `PORT_OFFSET` are legitimate (an `export`, a read in a test or an echo) and teach the filter, or to keep the refusal and document it next to the filter.

## Related

KS-2079 (In Progress, PR 2070's own ticket), KS-1355 (In Review), KS-1558 (Done). F-2070-1 of the same pass is filed separately (Medium, a different file).

## Searched before filing

Board, includeArchived, title and description and every comment of each open candidate; controls pass. `PORT_OFFSET` 1 open hit (KS-2079, gate 224's notes, not this finding); `check-compose-stack-safety` 2 open hits (KS-1355, KS-2079), neither holds it; `F-2070-2` 0.

title: Launcher census refuses an exec-only script: start, stop, kill, rm, pause and unpause match as any word after docker compose (F-2070-1)
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2070 (KS-2079, merged 2026-11-08T19:23:21Z as `5d6a95c552fd`) widened the platform-launcher census from the verbs `up|run|restart|down` to also `start|stop|kill|rm|pause|unpause`, and the new verbs match as ANY later whitespace-delimited word after `docker compose`, not as the compose subcommand. A committed script that only runs `docker compose exec api npm start` is therefore flagged as a platform launcher and refused with "A script runs the platform compose stack but is in neither list (KS-1355)". The same class already existed for `run`; the PR makes it six common words wider, on a guard that runs on the push path. No verdict changes on today's tree (the nine launchers are the same). Medium is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 106th, point 1, finding G243-F1).

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate243-tier2-batch/verdict.md`, finding F-2070-1 (Minor to Moderate) on PR 2070, head `0ae8aa98046c`, verdict GO WITH NOTES, accepted at merge.

## Evidence

MEASURED by the gate (it extracted the PR's own `_launcher_calls_compose` and ran one-line probes; positive control `docker compose up -d` FLAGGED):

* Flagged on the PR head, clean on develop before it: `docker compose exec api npm start`, `docker compose exec -T api pm2 stop all`, `docker compose exec api rm -rf /tmp/x`, `docker compose logs api rm`, `docker-compose exec api kill 1`.
* Develop already flagged `docker compose exec api npm run build` (the existing class for `run`).
* The suite `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` pins a bare `exec` and a word that merely STARTS with a verb ("startup"); it does not pin a verb as an argument of `exec`, so nothing fails on this.

READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `5d6a95c552fd`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`): the scope comment at line 133 lists the six new verbs; the `lit` regex at line 189 is `(^|[^-[:alnum:]_])docker([[:space:]]+|-)compose([^|;&#]*)[[:space:]](up|run|restart|down|start|stop|kill|rm|pause|unpause)([[:space:]]|$)`, whose `([^|;&#]*)` lets any text sit between `compose` and the verb; the variable-name branch at line 205 repeats the same alternation; the function `_launcher_calls_compose` is at line 212.

Effect: a launcher that only `exec`s into the stack must be sourced through the slot derivation or declared in `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS` with a ticket, a wrong-reason refusal. The guard runs on the push path and in the retired CI workflows.

## Fix shape

The verdict gives none. The gate's finding is the shape of the refusal; a fix needs a cell for "a verb as an argument of `exec`" first, because the suite does not pin it today.

## Related

KS-2079 (In Progress, PR 2070's own ticket; it holds gate 224's notes, not this finding), KS-1355 (In Review, the slot-derivation parent), KS-1558 (Done, the census this widened). F-2070-2 of the same pass is filed separately (Low, a different file).

title: SDK package: its test command runs vitest with no test files and exits 1; --passWithNoTests makes it 0 (measured on a scratch copy)
description:

Seat T 17th reported it (wrap mail of 2026-11-08 19:03Z); the board seat reproduced it on a scratch copy of the package. Low, as Wednesday ruled (ANSWER of 2026-11-08 19:21Z).

## Evidence

* MEASURED by the board seat (2026-11-08, about 19:30Z): a scratch copy of the package's nine files fetched at develop `6c9a593df4ab` (`Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript`: README, manifest, `src/client.ts`, `src/index.ts` and five files under `src/modules/`; none test-like), run with the monorepo's installed vitest 4.1.10, no arguments, no terminal, CI unset: "No test files found, exiting with code 1", exit 1. With CI set to true: the same, exit 1. Control: the same run with `--passWithNoTests`: exit 0, so the exit 1 comes from the missing test files.
* The limit of that measurement: the SDK declares vitest `^1.0.4` (line 40 of its manifest), not 4.1.10, and its own install was not done. Whether vitest 1.x behaves the same is UNMEASURED.
* READ ONLY, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`: the directory listings of `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript`, `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src` and `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src/modules` hold no name with test or spec in it and no vitest config.
* UNMEASURED: whether anything aggregates package test scripts and would run this one.

## Why it matters

title: systemTest format gate: the line-730 selection pipe may close early on GNU grep and select no package on a large push (gate 247 F74-1)
description:
**BLUF:** `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh` line 730 selects packages with `printf '%s\n' "$changed_paths" | grep "^systemTest/${p}/" > /dev/null`. On the macOS host that works. Gate 247 recalls that GNU grep treats output to `/dev/null` like `-q` and stops at the first match. If so, on Linux the pipe closes early, the pipeline returns 141 under `pipefail`, the package reads as not selected, and the gate exits 0 at line 739 without a word. The GNU premise is the gate's memory and is UNMEASURED. First step: measure the line-730 form on Linux with GNU grep. Medium is Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER to B 104th, PR 2074 notes).

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate247-tier1-tests-tooling/verdict.md`, finding F74-1 (Major, conditional) on PR 2074 (KS-1728 batch 2, merged as `15dca468b86f`). The gate says it is not a reason to hold that PR. The verdict's label is F74-1; the fleet's shorthand "G247-F1" names this finding and also PR 2069's F69-1, so this ticket uses the verdict's label.

## Evidence

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by the gate (macOS, `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD, the only grep on that host): a wrapper `grep` on PATH that adds `-q` only when stdout is `/dev/null`. With a 1.1 MB changed list, real grep gives exit 1, REFUSED, 3 of 3; the wrapper gives exit 0 with no refusal, 3 of 3; a one-path control gives exit 1, REFUSED. So if a grep behaves like the wrapper, the gate goes silently green.
* UNMEASURED: that GNU grep behaves like the wrapper. No GNU grep was available to the gate.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`): line 730 is as quoted; lines 737 to 740 take `selected` empty to `exit 0` with the comment "nothing under a gated package — say nothing, cost nothing". `.githooks/pre-push` lines 375 to 380 speak of Linux and dash, so the hook contemplates Linux pushers.
* The failure needs a grep that stops early and a changed list larger than the pipe buffer. The gate rates the likelihood low on today's macOS pushers, where it does not occur (measured).
* The census behind KS-1728 cannot find this form, because its regex looks for `-q`.

## History

KS-1716 (Done) proposed this exact form as the "read to EOF" fix for the original `grep -q` loss and measured it (3 of 3 runs selected all five packages); the ticket names a 64 KiB macOS pipe buffer and never mentions GNU grep. PR 2074 converted twelve other product lines to the same form. The same measurement also settles F74-2 (the statement "grep reads to EOF" stated without its condition), which Wednesday recorded on the PR without a ticket.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

After the measurement: if GNU grep stops early, select without a writer process (a pure-bash `case` match on the list, as KS-1716 notes PS-1254 did) and add a cell over a path list larger than the pipe buffer on a platform that stops early. If GNU grep reads to EOF, record the measurement here and close.

title: pre-push hook: a failing git diff reads as no change and the hook exits 0 before leg 1, so a RED commit pushes (gate 263 G1)
description:
**BLUF:** The real pre-push hook treats a failing `git diff` as an empty change set. With `git config diff.orderFile` naming a missing file, `git diff` exits 128 with no output, the changed set stays empty, and the hook exits 0 before leg 1: a RED commit pushes with rc 0 and no preflight line. Gate 263 measured this on the hook fixture at `35bcfa000`; the same lines are on develop `6c9a593df4ab`. High is Wednesday's call.

Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-09_gate263-tier1-x8-prerun-driver-r3/verdict.md`, finding G1 (a note outside the tool under test, which the gate calls the most important thing it found). Not a PR-merge item: it waits on no PR. A build seat fixes the hook; this ticket only records it.

## What was measured, and what was only read

* MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 263 (scratch worlds, local bare origins): `git config diff.orderFile <missing file>` makes `git diff` exit 128 with empty output, while `status`, `rev-parse` and `merge-base` still exit 0. The gate probed 17 `diff.*` and `core.*` faults and found this one shape. The real hook fixture, called directly with a new-branch stdin line on a RED commit: with the fault, rc 0 and "Blockchain/Dev changes detected" is never printed; without the fault, rc 1, the preflight ran and failed. Evidence in the gate folder: `evidence/order.out`, produced by `evidence/g263_order.py`.
* On the same fault the pre-run tool (X 8th's) still runs the preflight, so the pre-run path is stronger than the hook here.
* READ ONLY (the board seat, at develop `6c9a593df4ab`; I did not run the hook): in `.githooks/pre-push`, lines 129, 143 and 252 end `|| true` after `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only ...`. Line 251 sets `_informative=1` before the diff at line 252, so the KS-882 branch at line 271 (every base contains HEAD, run unconditionally) does not fire. With `changed` empty, line 372 `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` returns success before the preflight message at line 374. These are the lines the gate cited at `35bcfa000`; the gate's fixture hook is not necessarily develop's current hook, and the lines match.

## Why it is the same class as two fixed holes

The hook's own comments record KS-854 (lines 156 to 160: an unresolvable base left `changed` empty and the hook returned success before leg 1) and KS-882 (lines 181 to 187, banner at line 272: a base equal to HEAD gave an empty diff and the same exit). Both fixes treat "cannot compute" as "run the preflight" (lines 276 to 277 and 284 to 285 set `changed` to an unconditional marker and `st_all=1`). A diff that fails is the same case: an uncomputable change set is not a clean one.

## Fix shape (READ ONLY, not applied)

Capture the diff's exit status at lines 129, 143 and 252 instead of discarding it with `|| true`; on a non-zero status take the KS-854 and KS-882 path (banner, unconditional marker, `st_all=1`). Regression test: in a scratch repo set `diff.orderFile` to a missing path, push a RED commit, expect rc 1 and the "changes detected" line; the same push without the fault expects the same result.
